name: Artificer

Artificer Archetypes

Blaster (Artificer Archetype)

Reagentwright (Artificer Archetype)
Saboteur (Artificer Archetype)

Wand Adept (Artificer Archetype)

The artificer is a master of magic items. They find ways to use magic items in ways others can only dream of and how to instill magic into objects and constructs. Wands, potions, scrolls are all the ammunition in the arsenal of the artificer. Artificers adventure for a variety of reasons. Some seek new magic items to tinker with or empower themselves, others seek to test the items they have already created.

Class Details

Role: The role of the artificer is typically as a support caster, but can fill the role as an offensive caster depending upon the magic items they focus on.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d6

Starting Wealth: 3d6 × 10 gp (average 105 gp.) Additionally, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The artificer’s class skills are: Appraise (Int), Craft (Int), Disable Device (Int), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier

Class Features

The following are the class features of the artificer.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Artificers are proficient with simple weapons, light and medium armor, and shields, although not tower shields. Artificer spellcasting is not impeded by the armor worn or shield equipped so long as they are proficient with them.

Artifact Knack (Ex)

Beginning with 1st level, an artificer can identify magic items and recognize their magic auras without casting detect magic so long as they touch the object. Additionally, the artificer can take 10 or 20 on the check to identify the properties of the item and they add 1/2 their class level to Use Magic Device checks to magic items for which they have identified the properties.

Spells or effects that change or disguise magic auras can fool the artificer as well. However, the artificer is entitled to a Will save against such effects as if they had cast identify.

Magical Artisan (Ex)

At 1st level, the artificer reduces the increase to the DC of creating a magic item for not meeting one of the creation requirements by 1/2 their class level to a minimum of a +0 increase to the DC.

Spell Casting

An artificer casts arcane spells drawn from the artificer spell list. An artificer must choose and prepare their spells ahead of time.

To learn, prepare, or cast a spell, the artificer must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against an artificer’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the artificer’s Intelligence modifier.

An artificer can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on the table below. Additionally, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Intelligence score.

To cast a spell, the artificer must touch an object held or worn by a creature to affect them or the affected object if the spell targets objects. If the spell has a range further than touch, it is reduced to touch. Additionally, if a spell affects multiple targets, all affected targets must be touched. If the object the spell is cast upon is dropped or destroyed, the spell effects cease to benefit the bearer and in the case of destruction, the spell ends entirely. If the object is not destroyed and picked up by the same or another creature, the spell effects resume. If the spell creates a field or area, it is around the touched object and continues to work if separated from the original holder. Otherwise, this acts as normal spells. For example, a necklace with bull’s strength cast upon it can be dropped, then later picked up by another creature, granting the second creature the spell’s effects. However, the time when the amulet was not worn still counts against the duration of the bull’s strength spell.

Symbol or rune spells are treated as normal.

An artificer may know any number of spells. They must choose and prepare their spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying their spellbook. While studying, the artificer decides which spells to prepare.

Spellbooks: An artificer must study their spellbook each day to prepare their spells. They cannot prepare any spell not recorded in their spellbook except for read magic, which all artificers can prepare from memory. An artificer begins play with a spellbook containing all 0-level artificer spells plus three 1st-level artificer spells of their choice. The artificer also selects a number of additional 1st-level artificer spells equal to their Intelligence modifier to add to their spellbook. At each new artificer level, they gain two new artificer spells of any spell level or levels that they can cast (based on their new artificer level) for their spellbook. At any time, an artificer can also add spells found in other spellbooks to their own.

An artificer can learn spells from a wizard’s spellbook, just as a wizard can from an artificer’s spellbook. The spells learned must be on the artificer spell list, as normal. An alchemist can learn formulae from an artificer’s spellbook, if the spells are also on the alchemist spell list. An artificer can also learn spells from an alchemist so long as the formula is on the artificer spell list.

Cantrips: An artificer can prepare a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, each day, as noted on the table below. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again.

Reminder About Touch Spells

“You must touch a creature or object to affect it. A touch spell that deals damage can score a critical hit just as a weapon can. A touch spell threatens a critical hit on a natural roll of 20 and deals double damage on a successful critical hit. Some touch spells allow you to touch multiple targets. You can touch up to 6 willing targets as part of the casting, but all targets of the spell must be touched in the same round that you finish casting the spell. If the spell allows you to touch targets over multiple rounds, touching 6 creatures is a full-round action.”

It is recommended that players with an artificer character also familiarize themselves with using touch spells in combat; see page 185 to 186 of the Core Rulebook for more details.

Scribe Scroll

At 1st level, an artificer gains Scribe Scroll as a bonus feat.

Trapfinding (Ex)

At 1st level, the artificer adds 1/2 their level to Perception skill checks made to locate traps and to Disable Device skill checks (minimum +1). An artificer can use Disable Device to disarm magic traps.

Research Breakthrough

At 2nd level, and every even level thereafter, the artificer gains a bonus item creation feat, feat that helps in Use Magic Device or Craft skill checks, or other feat that deals with using, wielding, or making magic items. The artificer must meet the prerequisites of the feat chosen.

Assurance (Ex)

At 3rd level, the artificer can take 10 on Craft checks, if they so choose.

At 10th level, this also extends to all Spellcraft checks even if danger or distraction would prevent them from using the skill. At 17th level, this also extends to Use Magic Device.

Bonus Metamagic Feat

At 3rd level, an artificer gains a bonus metamagic feat for which they meet the prerequisites. The artificer gains an additional bonus metamagic feat at 9th and 15th levels.

Expert Crafter (Ex)

At 4th level, all time required to progress in item crafting, magical or mundane, is reduced by half. Additionally, any progress on mundane items is doubled, even with the reduced time.

Retain Charge (Su)

At 5th level, an artificer can choose to expend one of their prepared spells in lieu of expending a charge when activating a spell-trigger or spell-completion magic item, so long as they have a spell slot of the same spell level as the spell in the item. If the spell level is unclear, use the spell-like ability guidelines.

This can be combined with metamagic spell-trigger or metamagic spell-completion if a spell slot is expended that would equal the spell level of the charge being expended plus the metamagic feat.

Instilled Trinket Usage (Su)

At 6th level, an artificer can activate spell-completion and spell-trigger items using their own caster level and spell save DC modifiers.

Metamagic Spell-Trigger (Su)

Beginning with 7th level, an artificer can apply any metamagic feat they possess to a spell-trigger item as they activate it. However, this consumes an additional charge or use per day per level increase of the metamagic feat and they must possess the item creation feat for the item being modified. This does not take any additional time to activate. If the item only has one charge or use per day, they cannot use this ability, unless they can reduce the metamagic spell level, see below.

At 13th level, the artificer can reduce the charge cost for the use of this ability by 1. However, they must make a Fortitude save DC 15 + the original spell level + the original metamagic feat level increase or be fatigued. This cannot reduce the charge cost below 1 and cannot be used if the artificer is fatigued.

At 19th level, the artificer can instead reduce the charges cost by 2, but the DC is increased to 25 + the original spell level + the original metamagic feat level increase or be fatigued. This cannot reduce the cost below 1 and cannot be used if the artificer is fatigued.

Metamagic Spell-Completion (Sp)

Beginning with 11th level, an artificer can apply any metamagic feat they possess to a spell-completion item while activating it. To do so, they must possess the item creation feat for the item modified and must make a Use Magic Device check of 20 + 3 times the spell level modified by the metamagic feat. So, for example, an empowered burning hands would be 20 + (3 x 3) for a DC of 29. The artificer can use this ability a number of times equal to 3 + their Intelligence modifier. On a failure, the spell is expended as normal from the spell-completion item without the additional benefit but the use of the ability is expended. This Use Magic Device attempt is separate from such a check needed to activate the item in general.

Master Artificer (Ex)

At 20th level, all time required to progress in item crafting, magical or mundane, is reduced to 1/4. Additionally, any progress on mundane items is quadrupled, even with the reduced time. Additionally, they can use their retain charge ability once per day without expending a spell slot. However, they must make a Fortitude save DC 10 + twice the spell level or be fatigued.

Adding More Spells to the Artificer Spell List

Already included in the spell list above are all the 1PP spells and spells from our major books. In general, if you would like to add more 3PP spells to the list, err on the side of spells that add protections, empower abilities or attacks, affect items, or that follow themes in the established spells above. As always, consult your GM before adding spells or even using the spells in the list above. We always encourage adding more spells and having fun, but make sure everyone in your group is having fun, including your GM.
